title: Rex proclamation, scrapbook reflections and recent work
summary: Riddick shows a Rex 1967 proclamation, a recording with Johnny Wiggs, and says the scrapbook's satisfaction is having been there; he still wants to work.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: On a proclamation. Rex King of Carnival. This was given to me, you know, playing on Rex bandwagon. Rex 1967. Uh huh. Sure with Manjapanie. Sure with Manjapanie. Had the band. 된 stuff... 된 stuff... 된 stuff... 된 stuff...

된 stuff... 된 stuff... next 1967. Sherwood Mangiapani had the band. Now this is a recording if ever I cease to love. Music by Rene Luop Society Orchestra. Dr. Edmond Sushan. Now I made a recording on this also with Johnny Wiggs. That seems to be the crop. Pretty good crop. Did you do all the clipping or did your wife make the clippings for you? Don't you know if my wife had made it it would have been in order. But I showed it to so many people you know and everything. It's just all most possible. But someday one of my children maybe or one of my grandchildren or one of my great-grandchildren may take it and make something nice out of it. All the satisfaction that I got out of it was that I was there. It was a good feeling. So many of them today you can walk up to the band and they turn up their nose at you because they say to themselves, I'm working and you're not. I have already done the work. I don't have to work anymore. I saved my money and invested in it and I don't have to work anymore. Well that's good. That's a good feeling too, honey. Must be. But I still want to work as much as anybody will call me. I worked at, since I saw you last, I worked a very lovely brunch party out at Chateau Estates by myself. Then I worked at Preservation since I saw you all last.
